note: Captured from the GitHub Actions `overhead` job (ubuntu-latest, Python 3.13, CPU-only). Values are the max of two consecutive CI runs on the release branch to absorb runner jitter; +20% regression tolerance is applied at test time. Only CI-runner numbers belong in this file; a developer machine's numbers would set the gate to the wrong hardware. Mixed provenance: the three per-primitive micro-benchmarks were captured on 2026-08-04 from runs 754302d and 8cb83db, and the top-level generated_at/platform/python describe that capture. The two reference-loop ratios still carry their 2026-04-23 capture on Python 3.13.13 and kernel 6.17.0-1010; they are deliberately not regenerated here because the reference loop's run-to-run variance currently exceeds the tolerance it enforces, so regenerating them would ratify noise. See issue #73, which re-captures them once the sampling is fixed. Regenerate procedure: tests/overhead/README.md.
